newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan hopes U.N. will reconsider air embargo.
newsitem.headline: Sudan hopes U.N. will reconsider air embargo.

text.p: Sudan is hoping that the United Nations' delaying of a decision on whether to impose an air embargo against Khartoum will give the world body time to reconsider the move, a Sudanese official said on Saturday.

"Sudan hopes the delay will be a chance for weighing facts so that a fair resolution...will be adopted by the Security Council," the official Sudan news agency SUNA quoted Mustafa Othman Ismail, the state minister at the Foreign Ministry, as saying.

The U.N. Security Council on Thursday delayed for a month a decision on implementing an air embargo against Sudan for failing to extradite three men wanted for an attempt to kill Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Addis Ababa last year.
Sudan is already the target of mandatory diplomatic and travel sanctions that went into effect on May 10.
The Sudanese government says it has complied with Security Council resolutions and provided all information available but says Egypt and Ethiopia have not cooperated.
"Sudan has condemned all forms of terrorism. We have always condemned the assassination attempt on the life of President Mubarak," Ismail was quoted as saying.
